intro: VTT to SRT turns WebVTT subtitles (.vtt), the ones downloaded from websites, video platforms and online courses, into SubRip (.srt), the most compatible format: VLC, Windows Media Player, smart TVs, Plex, Kodi and video editors such as Premiere, DaVinci Resolve or CapCut all read it.
Timings, line breaks, italics, bold, underline and strikethrough are kept, and subtitles are renumbered in order. WebVTT NOTE, STYLE and REGION blocks, which are not subtitles, are discarded.
WebVTT position settings (align, position, line, size) and speaker names (<v Ana>) do not exist in SRT: they are lost and we warn you. Entities such as & are turned back into their character.

The conversion runs on our server: subtitles are read with pysubs2, a widely used free library for this job, and the new file is written in UTF-8 and sorted by time. We detect the original's encoding, so old subtitles in Windows-1252, with all their accents, come out right. You can convert up to 20 files at once and download them together in a ZIP.
steps: Choose whether to keep the text styling.

faq.q: Will the SRT work on my TV?
faq.a: Almost certainly: it is the most widespread subtitle format. Give it the same name as the video (movie.mp4 and movie.srt) so it loads automatically.
They keep their timings and are sorted by when they start; most players show them at the same time.

faq.q: Can I convert a WebVTT with CSS styles?
faq.a: Yes, but styles in the STYLE block have no equivalent in SRT and are not copied.
